blocking_findings.consequence: The primary result is not reproducible from the 6,144 games; analysts could choose a favorable aggregation or success interpretation after seeing outcomes.
blocking_findings.required_resolution: Before formal registration, state the exact primary statistic, cluster-resampling unit and interval, and whether the comparison is descriptive or has a directional success rule. Keep the alternative statistic secondary.
blocking_findings.trigger: The primary is named “Paired Q1 difference” on shared seeds, but the estimator is not defined. It could mean the difference between each model’s marginal bottom-quartile mean, or the bottom-quartile mean of per-seed paired differences. Those are distinct statistics and can differ. The 2,000 bootstrap draws have a seed but no registered resampling unit or interval/decision rule.

checks: Checkpoint420, model and Adam reuse, architecture, reward, accepted pool, one pair, and no-promotion boundary agree across the reviewed artifacts.

Frame target arithmetic is coherent: 180 * 64 slots * 256 K4 decisions * 4 frames = 11,796,480 frames per arm. Whole-vector-call retention bounds K4 overshoot below 256 and K1 overshoot below 64 frames.
Evaluation count reconciles: 3 models * 2 repeat settings * 1,024 shared D9 seeds = 6,144 games. Primary uses the same K1 sampled controller for both final checkpoints; K4 is secondary.

The design explicitly preserves fixed final-frame checkpoints, no best-interim selection, true termination/live bootstrap requirements, and actual optimizer-step reporting. These controls fit the stated question.
limits: No source-specific verdict. Implementation, gradient-accumulation equivalence, stream capacity, reward aggregation, terminal handling, resource qualification, D9 freshness, and launch gates require later pinned reviews.

nonblocking_limits.detail: One matched pair is one trajectory comparison. Shared pairseed aligns initial states, but subsequent environment, policy, and RNG paths diverge; it does not provide common random numbers or training-seed uncertainty. Interpret evaluation-seed intervals as conditional on these two trained checkpoints.

Equal gameplay-frame exposure is registered and the 11,796,480-frame target equals 180 K4 update-equivalents beyond checkpoint420. The treatment also changes gamma/lambda, rollout length, and effective minibatch to preserve nominal game-time cadence. Report the effect as a matched-frame training-recipe bundle, not an isolated action-repeat effect. The unchanged .01 entropy coefficient is correctly scoped to the averaged per-decision PPO loss; do not claim fourfold entropy force.

The gamma/lambda fourth-root values match decay across four-frame decision boundaries. If the K4 collector supplies an undiscounted sum of within-call rewards, this is not exact per-raw-frame reward discounting inside each four-frame call. Confirm reward aggregation semantics in the later frozen source review before claiming identical game-time objectives.

The 9-hour cap relies on extrapolated K1 cost. The registered real 8-update-per-arm qualification, capped at 1,800 seconds and 6 GiB, must pass before formal registration; then recalibrate full training plus 6,144-game evaluation. D9 remains proposed and must be reserved before use. Preserve D7/D8/D9 exclusions from training and evaluation.

scope: Read-only review of the three frozen parent design artifacts. No changing successor source inspected; no ledger, checkpoint, seed outcomes, native runtime, MPS, Torch, games, or training accessed.
